Comments (English): [ Awkward design ] || ---------------- || I hate this dishwasher. It gets dishes clean, on the plus side, but is extremely hard to load. The pins on the lower rack are completely vertical, so that fragile dishes have a good chance of flopping around when sliding the rack into the dishwasher. The upper rack's pins are so close together, that it's impossible to put ordinary drinking glasses or mugs in without putting them over the pins. The installer told us we should never use the soap dispenser, since we use the action packs or tablets. What's up with that? Why is the dispenser not designed to use those tablets, and dispense them at the correct part of the cycle. Now, I don't know if the tablet is all dissolved before the cycle actually starts. In addition, I can't see if the Rinse Aid dispenser has anything in it or not. I've looked online to see if there is a guide for how to properly load this dishwasher, but all I've found is pictures of lots of plates on the lower rack, and glassware on the upper rack. I need to see how to load a mix of plates, bowls, mugs, pots pans, and the normal day-to-day kitchenware.

Comments (English): [ Solid Performer, But Some Annoyances ] || ---------------- || Solid Performer. I know some folks have complained about the plastics drying, but that has not been my experience for the most part. I had an excellent Kenmore prior, and this one seems to be outperforming it. Especially in drying and drying plastics. A couple of dozen cycles, mostly auto, a couple of heavy and a pot wash (and some glassware cleaning for the holidays) and one hour washes (which does really well in an hour). Some "dirty" meals and dishes for a household of 6. Never the Normal cycle/wash (so perhaps that makes a difference for some ppl? ). Sparkling and usually very dry. I get the feeling the heat is on when it isn't even in dry mode and using just ambient heat (the timer is counting down? Why not make the cycle look shorter by 10 minutes. I'll open the door, if I don't dry mode is on, right? err. ) Auto clean most things, but I am used to seeing the time go up or down, I haven't seen that happen. I have noticed the temp go up though. Boo-boos? The cutlery basket has no back that my less expensive Kenmore had. If you make the mistake of putting longer knives or long utensils on the outside edge and shut the door, it might not close if they catch the edge of the unit wall I think the racks hold more, but I am used to symmetrical ranks and this one take a little more thinking and redo-ing for me. Smooooooth rolling wheels, too smooth in fact. Sometimes they slide out as you open the door and it is level. Remote Start you have to pre-plan and push a button to enable it (and I guess load it first too? Make it load for me. anyway. I don't get remote start. Delayed, sure). This is a silly feature and would have preferred and extra download cycle. LG Documentation stinks. One more time. The LG cycle documentation and latest tech innovation for the quad wash pro stinks. Other manufactures have far more details about their cycles and download cycles and what they do and take (water, time, settings, etc). How there latest greatest gimmick will work. Here? how heavy is different from casserole wash is anyone's guess (and temp and water usage). Steam got a so-so debut years ago, but it is still used here. The technical specs really on the web site could tout it or set the real expectations of how it is best used. That said, it was used with the glassware, they were stunning. Same for the QuadWash Pro vs QuadWash original. I will buy into micro bubbles because of the extra mechanical action from them hitting the food and exploding, but I just told you more than LG did about how and why they work (I can't imagine how you demo it). But these details make the product easier to use and use right and get a good review. In general I would not wonder if something was "off"--still not sure if Auto is busted if the timing never goes down and the manual does list 98 minutes on the low end and 3 hours on the high). Or is it just sloppy documentation and it covers all models the same way (so something else is 98 minutes) If it weren't for the basket and the documentation, this might have been a 4.5 or 5, but I had to hold back a star for some of these.

Sentence (English): I really wanted a dishwasher for my home, but since it's an older apartment and a rental, I simply couldn't fit a 12-place setting one.
Comments (English): I really wanted a dishwasher for my home, but since it's an older apartment and a rental, I simply couldn't fit a 12-place setting one. So, after much deliberation, I ended up buying a 6-place setting model. There was an LG 6-place model available, but the door opening looked a bit inconvenient, and it didn't seem like it would fit as much inside as the Samsung. Actually, this one was famous as a hot deal on mom cafes, and looking at the users, everyone had great reviews. Dishwashers are usually expensive, but I don't know why, but this product was really cheap, so I'm satisfied! Considering the value for money, I think it's definitely the right choice to get one. We are a family of three, so we manage just fine, but I do think it might be a bit overwhelming on days when we cook or have a lot of side dishes. Still, for this price and performance, I'm extremely satisfied! As a dual-income household, doing the dishes in the morning was so hard. Dinner was the same! I'd come home completely exhausted, but I'd still be doing the dishes. The kid would whine to play, I'd be tired, I'd have to help with the kids' homework, and fold the laundry. There's just so much to do... Being freed from just one dishwashing task has completely changed my quality of life. To those of you who aren't getting a dishwasher yet... why on earth aren't you getting one? Please, please, please get one. It’s just so good. Now, no one has to fight with their husband over the dishes anymore. Also, this one is really well divided into compartments, and the shelves are well organized so you can fit a lot of dishes. It even has four cutlery holders, so it’s great for filling up every side. I'm still not sure which products can't be put in the dishwasher, so that's a bit tricky, but I'll learn hard and try using it. Oh! Since the product requires a water inlet hose, you need to drill a hole about 1 centimeter deep in the sink. You can run the hose for drainage to the side of the sink, but you have to make a hole just for the water inlet hose. If you're renting, the landlord's permission is a must.

Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Series Dishwasher (SHP78CM5N) Review ] || ---------------- || We purchased our dishwasher about a month ago, and we couldn't be happier with our selection. First, the dishwasher cleans extremely well, even cheesy egg mess that we'd have normally pre-washed/soaked, comes out clean. The power wash function seems to perform very well. This dishwasher is extremely quiet. Our prior dishwasher wasn't really loud, but we can't believe how quiet this one is. The heating/drying is excellent. Only items that have a lip on the top, that allow water to pool, retain any moisture. The ability to customize the racks is excellent, including the tilt feature that further helps keep water from pooling. The top rack was our surprise, in that we thought we would remove it, to gain extra space for the 2nd rack, but we use the top rack for silverware, and that frees space in the bottom, as we don't use the silverware caddy. The clean design of the face is very nice (we opted for no handle), and the controls are on the top, again, keeping the face of the door very clean. Overall we are extremely happy with our purchase, and really enjoy using this dishwasher.

And since that doesn't even address the water getting in I am going to junk it instead of spending more money to find whatever circuit is messed up. What a shame. Not worth the money. This is the shortest life of any expensive appliance I have ever bought.

Sentence (English): I bought a Haier W30, opened the door to dry it, washed a pot every day, and kept trying various modes.
Comments (English): I bought a Haier W30, opened the door to dry it, washed a pot every day, and kept trying various modes. I even got a good deal on dishwashing salt~ If you see the price in the second picture, don’t hesitate and buy it directly! Dishwashing supplies: dishwashing salt (for soft water) rinse agent (quick drying after adding) dishwashing powder (cleaning effect). The first two are added once and last for a long time. Sentence (English): Our previous Kitchenaid dishwasher failed after 2yr, so I bought a different model which also has the deep top rack we like.
Comments (English): [ UNRELIABLE: PUMP FAIL in 5 months ] || ---------------- || Our previous Kitchenaid dishwasher failed after 2yr, so I bought a different model which also has the deep top rack we like. Unfortunately, this one has failed, too, but at least within the warranty period. The first time it had an issue was 1 month after it was installed in our house, and at that time the technician concluded it was due to dishsoap in the machine. It worked OK after that one time. Four months later, it stopped working again. However, even with the warranty, first we waited 1wk for a technician to come diagnose our problem (bad sump pump), now another week waiting for a part to come in so he can replace it. This is all covered by the warranty, but no compensation for the 2+weeks of doing dishes ourselves, and we are a big family and cook every day. The other thing is the warranty work does not cover the technician pulling the unit out from under the counter for the work. We are supposed to do that ourselves, and put it back later, too, I guess. I either have to hire (pay) a plummer to come do this or figure it out for myself. So, don't think a warranty will protect you from this kind of inconvenience and cost. It is better to just buy a reliable product from the start, unless you have extra time to schedule (and be present for) repairs, do dishes by hand for 2weeks each time there is an issue, and by the way everything is NOT covered, like pulling the dishwasher out from your counter for the repair technician. What is up with that?

Sentence (English): The dishwasher does a really good job of cleaning the dishes (even really dirty ones! )
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher with one exception ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher does a really good job of cleaning the dishes (even really dirty ones! ) and is so quiet you can't even tell it's running. The only complaint we have, which gives this a 3-star rating, is that the "Auto-door Release" function that opens the door upon completion of the dry cycle only worked for a week then stopped. A service tech came out to replace the malfunctioning part, but it failed again after just 2 days(! ). As we otherwise like the dishwasher and don't want to go through the hassle of returning it and getting a different d/w, we decided to just keep it and will manually open the door when it's done like we did with our Bosch for the past 10 years. Samsung needs to rethink that feature and either eliminate it or redesign it as other reviewers on Costco reported this same problem. If that feature isn't important to you, this unit is excellent otherwise and was a great buy at the Costco sale price (at their regular price I'd recommend the comparably priced Bosch unit instead).

We had to replace our 12 yrs old dishwasher and went for a Bosch SHX53CM5N. Overall good quality/price ratio. Had to find a dishwasher that I could fit into my cabinet which has a drain protruding bout 1cm above foor level to the left side. This dishwasher has 3 adjustable legs 2 in front and one in middle at the back, so I was able to level it above the protruding drain and problem solved. It is necessary to use the wifiApp to benefit the full potentiel of this dishwasher which provide additional programs and options to the simplied control panel. Note that once the program is selected and the door is closed, whitout the home connect app, the only guide you have is a red light projected on the floor that indicate the program is running. So it has been 2 weeks now and so far so good. The only negative point is the wine glass support notch which are to small for many type of glass wine which make it difficult to stand whitout moving.

Sentence (English): Hard to know where to start!
Comments (English): [ Two Drawer Cafe Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Hard to know where to start! There is so much to love about the two drawer. First of all it cleans everything to perfection from stuck on cheese on utensils, to pots, pans, and glass wear is sparkling clean. I use Cascade pods and never have a problem with residue. It drains completely and I Never have water sitting on the bottom of the drawer. I love the knock idea to stop DW if I need to add an item and push the start button again and close the door and it starts up again. Loading the dishwasher is key. I never over crowd. The settings are easy to follow and learn. Upper drawer is large than lower drawer, and I like that. Mostly I run the upper with glasses, mugs, bowls, utensils, and plates on the normal setting and Lower drawer for pots and pans on the pot settings. Two drawers at different settings! Love it! When the DW is completed, there's a chime, but I usually can't hear it, would be nice if I could turn up the volume or an indicator light showing it's finished. I was hesitant to purchase Cafe Two drawer from the negative reviews. Honestly, I believe the reason why is,,,Installed incorrectly, causing dishwasher not to drain properly. Hot water temperature too low, causing unclean dishes and residue. Over crowding dishes Using too much powder. I suggest sticking to pods. Gel, or powder. I do have a major complaint. Dishwasher install recommended 4 screws to secure into the side of the cabinets. After only one week, wood is split and dishwasher rocks when opening. I believe the is a GE flaw that needs to be addressed quickly. I have installer coming today to fix it. Hopefully it holds up before I need to replace cabinets. Overall, I'm really smitten with the Two Drawer Cafe

I have a hole about the size of a 500-won coin at home, but since I put in the gas hose and water purifier, there wasn't enough space, so I bought the no-drill model. It comes with a drilling stencil, so it's nice that I can drill a hole later. Here are the very honest, objective downsides of a product I bought with my own money:  - You have to be good at Tetris. They say it gets easy once you get used to it, but maybe because it's my first time, it takes a long time. It's surprisingly stressful when things don't fit in properly. I was tidying up and dropped a knife, and I freaked out when it stuck into the floor. I still can't Tetris well; I think to myself, "By this time, I would have already finished the dishes."  - Sometimes it doesn't clean properly. Or there is a thick layer of white detergent powder. I used the powerful wash cycle, but I have to wipe it again every time this happens. I wonder if I can't control the detergent amount.  - It takes too long. I can't use the dishes I need right away. Washing for two hours... By this time, I would have finished the dishes myself. - You have to pre-wash. Don't get your hands wet? You have to. Pros: - It opens automatically so it dries on its own, leaving no water or water stains. It gives a sparkling, squeaky clean feeling that is on a whole different level compared to wiping by hand. - It saves time and is convenient when there are a lot of dishes. Maybe because it has only been a few days, I don't really know if it's amazing yet. For now, the biggest advantage for me is that it doesn't leave the water stains and moisture typical of hand washing. ++++++ 1 week. I've gotten a bit better at Tetris. Since we are a two-person household, I gather everything up and run it all at once; because I only use the dishes I always use, I've become more skilled at figuring out locations and arranging them. Cake grease, meat grease, red broth... I used to sigh just looking at them, but now it's so convenient. At first, you might wonder why you bought this, but you definitely need to use it to get better. It's so convenient. However, sometimes the detergent dispenser doesn't open and doesn't dissolve. It's annoying. I don't know why that happens, so I have to clean the dispenser, wipe it down again, put it in, and run it. Even though it doesn't require drilling, I don't really find it cumbersome. It's convenient because I always keep it handy next to the water tank; I just rinse it before use, plug in the hose, and fill it up.

Comments (English): [ Installation Embezzlement & Fraud Targeting Women ] || ---------------- || I have called multiple times and sadly, you are not able to speak to staff directly at your local Best Buy about the people they have whom install the dishwasher. Sentence (English): We really like the dishwasher in terms of quality, esthetics, and how clean it gets the dishes.
Comments (English): [ Really nice, just takes long and some noise inside ] || ---------------- || We really like the dishwasher in terms of quality, esthetics, and how clean it gets the dishes. We transitioned from a GE Profile in the same price range, and the Bosch machine is definitely nicer. The machine operation itself is very quiet, the top rack for utensils is extremely useful, and the bottom rack is laid out well for most dishes, bowls, pots, etc. letting us wash more dishes per load. However, for whatever reason it seems like we can't find a way to arrange lighter-weight items or Tupperware in the middle rack that doesn't cause more noise than what we had before. Either you can hear the water spraying against the plastic items, or the light-weight items get thrown around inside – overall more noise than what we had, unless we do ceramic/metal/heavy dishes only. Also, the wash cycles are quite long, with the fastest cycle still taking >1hr. The salesperson informed us this is because it's more energy efficient, which other neighbors have said about their newer dishwashers as well, but it still seems excessive. Other than those two gripes, we really like it.

Sentence (English): We got this dishwasher to replace an old frigidaire that finally went kaput.
Comments (English): [ Exceeded expectations! ] || ---------------- || We got this dishwasher to replace an old frigidaire that finally went kaput. We expected this to be similar but quieter. We were astounded how clean and perfect everything looked after the first wash! And to say it was quieter is an understatement! You can barely hear it! You need to be standing right next to it to hear anything! There is a red light it projects on the floor to let you know it is running. You can also track the cycle on the smartphone app. This dishwasher is loaded with features It has a built in water softener and a crystal dry system I have not seen from any other manufacturer. It works! Everything is bone dry, even plastic items. It has the 3rd upper level tray for silverware. I didn't think we'd make much use of it but just the opposite, its so convenient! In fact we removed the basket in the bottom tray to make more room for dishes since we don't need it anymore. I don't think we could ever go back to a dishwasher without that 3rd tray. One hiccup we had was that the dishwasher was not registering the fact that we filled the built in water softener compartment with dishwasher salt. It kept saying it was empty. I discovered via google that simply stirring the salt with a small plastic utensil can fix that issue. It did! The price was good considering the features. I highly recommend! Bosch has now spoiled me for all future dishwashers!

Sentence (English): Love this dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Beautiful dishwasher, practically silent ] || ---------------- || Love this dishwasher! It's so quiet, the only noise is from the air gap which has nothing to do with the dishwasher itself. The door opening near the end of the drying cycle is such a great feature as it really helps with drying, even Tupperware. Beautiful white glass front. Very clear maintenance instructions to easily clean out the drain filters periodically to maintain performance. Also “sings” at the end of the cycle, which is adorable. Be sure to follow the instruction to swap out the brass screw cap on the dishwasher elbow for the water intake with the plastic one provided to ensure a proper seal. Using a brass screw cap can more easily damage the threading and won't expand and contract at the same rate from the hot water which could cause leaking. Easy to swap out and had no issues. Be sure to get a dishwasher elbow that is curved, not a sharp 90 degree angle, to easily fit into the plastic screw cap.

Sentence (English): First of all, Costco needs to state in big bold letters that "INSTALLATION INCLUDED IS NOT AVAILABLE IN ALL AREAS".
Comments (English): [ Note to self:Read Full Reviews First! ] || ---------------- || First of all, Costco needs to state in big bold letters that "INSTALLATION INCLUDED IS NOT AVAILABLE IN ALL AREAS". I purchased this dishwasher first and appreciated that installation and haul-away of old unit was included in the price. It wasn't until viewing the order confirmation screen that I noted that installation was not available in my area. I could have backed out at that point, but I am a handyman and have installed several dishwashers, so no biggy. I've read several reviews now after our installation that state you cannot tell if the unit is running because the control pad is hidden. With ours, all you have to do is look at the floor and see the red light reflection in the lower right to know that the unit is on and going through its cycles. The bottom rack is not user friendly when loaded and it will tip into the valley created by the open door at the bottom if you're not careful, but if you learn to load and unload the bottom rack in a certain way, you can get around this. We bought this unit for a vacation home based on the Bosch we have in our permanent home that is 15 years old and still working well. However, these two dishwashers are not the same. It wasn't until viewing the order confirmation screen that I noted that installation was not available in my area. I could have backed out at that point, but I am a handyman and have installed several dishwashers, so no biggy. I've read several reviews now after our installation that state you cannot tell if the unit is running because the control pad is hidden. With ours, all you have to do is look at the floor and see the red light reflection in the lower right to know that the unit is on and going through its cycles. The bottom rack is not user friendly when loaded and it will tip into the valley created by the open door at the bottom if you're not careful, but if you learn to load and unload the bottom rack in a certain way, you can get around this. We bought this unit for a vacation home based on the Bosch we have in our permanent home that is 15 years old and still working well. However, these two dishwashers are not the same. The 100 is a very basic dishwasher and it is noisier than I expected. In fact, there is a hoarse little frog croaking in the upper left behind the door that is fairly audible. This isn't a deal breaker, but it wasn't expected either. The installation was somewhat of a challenge as the old unit was hardwired in and the new dishwasher was too tight up top, but I blame myself for that as I wasn't onsite to firsthand measure the unit that needed to be removed. Rather, I trusted specs found online for the old and new unit. Fortunately for me, the previous installer had used a 3/4" melamine spacer at the top to hide the gap above the old unit and I simply removed that to provide the extra room. The other installation issue was the old unit was hardwired in and the new unit came with a plug-in cord. So, I bought a single gang side-mount electrical box with offset ears on the side and attached that to one of the wood shipping slats that came with the new dishwasher. The wood slat attached vertically to the side of the cabinet deep inside the cavity with the box attached to the bottom of the slat down low, way in the back, and just above the floor. With the Romex coiled up in the back and zip tied off and a 20 amp receptacle installed in the electrical box mounted low on the slat, the unit was ready to be plugged in. I reused the old braided hot water supply line using ample plumbers tape and the installation was complete with no leaks! After what I went through on the electrical side, I don't blame Costco for not providing free installation here in Hawaii. Electrical codes are also different here. That said, everything is on "Hawaii time" here and if you want something done, you best do it yourself. In conclusion, we're still not certain we will keep this model, but given the average star rating between the three Bosch models offered on this site, this model makes the most sense to us for a vacation home. if you can learn to workaround a few of the design drawbacks stated here and deal with some potential installation issues, you will likely be satisfied with your purchase. Therefore, I would recommend to a friend, but only after they know all this.

I've had this maching for about two months, and do various size loads daily. All of the dishes, pots, and flatware come out spotless. I would definitely recommend this model, or any of the other diswashers made by BOSCH.

Sentence (English): We recently purchased the KitchenAid DW from Lowes.
Comments (English): [ We Bought A Lemon ] || ---------------- || We recently purchased the KitchenAid DW from Lowes. The person who installed it said he was getting an error message that there was a “Diverter Leak”. I immediately called the KitchenAid # I got from Lowes and they wanted me to try a few things (like the cable company does). Fortunately our installer was still here and told her he tried all the recommended solutions multiple times. I was then given a service window of 8:00 to 4:00 today, but fortunately the repair guy came out first thing. He replaced the defective part, but when I ran through the wash cycle and opened to DW door I got a strong burning smell. I could see something that looked like a cap that goes somewhere inside the unit and it was pretty melted. I called KitchenAid again, went through the issue and the guy sent me over to their Safety Dept. after about 20 minutes on hold I got someone, explained the situation and they are sending out another technician a week from now. I told her I don't feel safe with the machine and just want to return it, but that was a big no. Thanks Whirlpool / KitchenAid for selling me this lemon. I really appreciate it.

Comments (English): [ Terrible Customer Service from Lowe's ] || ---------------- || This review is not a judgement on the dishwasher itself, but a review of Lowe's absolutely horrendous customer service. Do yourself a favor and buy your appliances from Costco.

Sentence (English): We bought this to replace a 5 year old LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Sparkling dishes ] || ---------------- || We bought this to replace a 5 year old LG dishwasher. The LG had two major issues over the years: the control panel had to be replaced early on and finally the main motor assembly started smoking and causing error codes. We bought the Bosch based on its reputation for reliability and had the LG hauled away. We have moderately hard water so it was a pleasant surprise to find out this one also has a built-in water softener, which is usually a feature on the higher level Bosch dishwashers. The fact that it is connected to the internet means it can download software updates, which it did as soon as I connected the app. The app let's you change settings that would be much more difficult from the control panel like the water softener setting and rinse aid amount to use. It also lets you know when the rinse aid or water softener salt is running out. As for performance, our dishes have never looked so clean. Even though this model doesn't have the door opening feature like the 500 series, our dishes always come out spotless, including the plastics. I'm sure the rinse aid and water softener contribute to the drying performance. One area the LG struggled with was peanut butter on spoons or plates. So far the Bosch has completely removed peanut butter even on the speed cycle. I did the install myself. One thing to note is that this unit is quite a bit taller than the LG. It just barely managed to squeeze in to the space under my counter. This made the conventional top mount option impossible. Thankfully Bosch provides three options for mounting: conventional top mount with a metal bracket, side mount with metal bracket or a bracket-less alternative side mount. The alternative side mount was the only one that worked for me. It requires a 600mm spacing on the sides and a screw that goes right through a countersunk hole on the dishwasher itself. I was able to use two blocks of wood screwed into the cabinet frame leaving a 600mm wide space in the opening at the level of the screw holes. This mounting method worked perfectly and seems like a more solid mount than the conventional metal bracket method.

Sentence (English): Fantastic experience all the way around, beginning with the installation team sent to deliver & install the dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ WOW - JUST WOW! We Love It! ] || ---------------- || Fantastic experience all the way around, beginning with the installation team sent to deliver & install the dishwasher. Best Buy hit a home run with this team! Installation was free of any issues or difficulties - pretty straight forward. Our first run with the dishwasher was terrific! We opted not to get a new dishwasher with a 3rd rack - it was what we initially looked for, and were concerned that we'd be disappointed without one. but that is not the case. We love the roominess inside this Maytag dishwasher, and feel that all of our items fit - with air to spare. The prongs in the racks provide enough versatility to accommodate all types of dishes, glasses & utensils - we do not regret not getting the 3rd rack. The top rack is extremely roomy with a lot of "head room". The dishwasher was soooooo super quiet - not noise-free, but we didn't even realize it had stopped running when the cycle was done, it was so quiet (the dishwasher is literally 20 ft from our living room, where we were sitting).When the cycle is finished - it says "clean" on the panel. which is helpful. The dishes were not only spotless - but they were not super hot to touch (within 15 min of "clean" coming on the screen), and were completely dry - including our plastic lids and cups. FANTASTIC! In an age where appliances now play songs and have panels that look like an aircraft cockpit - you do NOT need any more than this very simple, very straight forward operating panel. Less to break, less to have to fiddle with, and just enough to give you some above-board options. The dishwasher is well made, sturdy & attractive. For a mid-price-range dishwasher, you will love this Maytag.

Sentence (English): This replaced an equivalent Kitchenaid (stainless steel interior and exterior) which worked very well for over 16 years.
Comments (English): This replaced an equivalent Kitchenaid (stainless steel interior and exterior) which worked very well for over 16 years. We replaced it because the plastic components inside were getting heat fatique and replacement parts would have been expensive. But the old Kuitchenaid was a reliable workhorse mechanically and owed us nothing.This new Kitchenaid is better than the previous one in being VERY quiet. It seems to clean gunked-up pots a bit better on the bottom rack , and the three-shelf arrangement allows more flexible and easier loading. There's definitely more interior space available. Items like serving utensils and kitchen knives clean well on the shallow top (3rd) rack. The Normal cycle seems to run a little long; we've experimented with the Express Wash and found it effective with normal dinner dishes. Dishes are dry at end of full cycle. Control buttons/lights are simple and straightforward. So far (about one month in including a lot of Thanksgiving cleanup) we're very satisfied. I installed the DW myself after HD's delivery, it was very straightforward into the existing standard DW space, hardwired, saving $250 and $50 disposal. If you have an outlet, you need to order a cord kit for this DW. HD had some delivery problems (drivers couldn't find our house due to their GPS malfunctioning) but the dispatcher and crew took an extra effort to get here so we didn't need to reschedule delivery. Bottom of carton was damp on delivery from water from factory testing - - delivery crew said this was normal, and the unit appeared totally new and unblemished, and I did find some residual water inside. Unpacking: the DW door was difficult to open out of box - - I thought I was possibly ignoring a shipping tab or a latch that needed removal - - but it was because the plastic PVC shipping liner between the door and gasket made it very tight - - just give it a good pull. Kitchenaid 800 customer service line actually reachable to confirm. Recommend watching the Kitchenaid installation video even if you're handy - - the tip to carefully score blue protective film on door before peeling it away made for a neater installation. Good performance and value so far, especially on sale at HD with free delivery and avoiding the installation charge.

We replaced it because the plastic components inside were getting heat fatique and replacement parts would have been expensive. But the old Kuitchenaid was a reliable workhorse mechanically and owed us nothing.This new Kitchenaid is better than the previous one in being VERY quiet. It seems to clean gunked-up pots a bit better on the bottom rack , and the three-shelf arrangement allows more flexible and easier loading. There's definitely more interior space available. Items like serving utensils and kitchen knives clean well on the shallow top (3rd) rack. The Normal cycle seems to run a little long; we've experimented with the Express Wash and found it effective with normal dinner dishes. Dishes are dry at end of full cycle. Kitchenaid 800 customer service line actually reachable to confirm. Recommend watching the Kitchenaid installation video even if you're handy - - the tip to carefully score blue protective film on door before peeling it away made for a neater installation.
